trigger: a C++ diff reaches review without its recorded resource ownership proof
summary: Resource Ledger, tree as fixed. No new fd, HANDLE, sqlite3*, sqlite3_stmt*, thread or heap allocation, and no new member. The stop signal is the existing agent-core latch yuzu::agent::subprocess_cancel_requested(): one process-lifetime std::atomic<bool> in the agent-core shared library (agents/core/src/subprocess_runner.cpp), which the loaded plugin links and reads, never unloaded before the plugin. The cancelled predicate is a std::function passed by const reference through purge_source and gc_dictionary, and gc_dictionary copies it into the stack ScopedProgressHandler, which clears the sqlite3 progress handler on every exit path (RAII), so no callback outlives the call. Tests own their second sqlite connection through SqliteHandleOwner (closed on every path), put the process-wide latch back through an RAII guard (StopLatch), and use yuzu_test_ temp directories. Lock order is unchanged: rollup_mu_ -> collect_mu_ -> software_collect_mu_ -> EchoDatabase::mu_, and the fold's op_mu_ is taken inside gc_dictionary only.
classification_rationale: the ledger this row records was the missing artefact

trigger: an agent stop while the weekly dictionary sweep (run_dictionary_gc) holds rollup_mu_ and the fold's op_mu_ for its 2 / 4 / 8 s deadline; shutdown waits behind it, up to 8 s instead of the former 2 s
summary: Found by six agents and the adversarial pass: the scheduled sweep passed no stop predicate. Fixed by passing the agent's stop latch (a plugin-local flag set in shutdown() would have been inert: the agent joins the trigger threads and the command pool before it calls shutdown()). Covered by a dispatcher test that raises the latch under an RAII guard.
classification_rationale: the stop poll the purge path had was missing from the scheduled path

trigger: a sweep or purge ended by an agent stop is recorded as starved (dict_gc_starved_total bumped; on the weekly path also the attempt stamp and streak), giving a false signal and a longer next deadline
summary: Fixed on both paths: purge_source reads the sticky latch once after the sweep and counts a starved sweep only when it was not stopped; run_dictionary_gc returns before any marker write when the latch is raised. Covered by the store test (starved total stays 0 after a stop) and the dispatcher test (total, streak and attempt stamp all read 0).
classification_rationale: a counter named starved was moved by a pass that was not starved

trigger: a purge's TRUNCATE checkpoint finds the log pinned; the maintenance pass then uses TRUNCATE only when it evicted rows or the log outgrew kEchoWalAllowanceBytes, else PASSIVE, which does not shrink the -wal file
summary: The comments and documents said the residue 'clears at the next checkpoint'. Wording fixed everywhere it appeared (code comment and log text, README, user manual, REST API reference, clock-guarded retention, dashboard note, changelog): the pages stay until a later checkpoint truncates the log, which a rerun of the purge does and reports, and which the maintenance pass does only when it evicts rows or the log outgrows its allowance. The automatic TRUNCATE retry and a status line for a pending log are not built; filed as #7987.
classification_rationale: the comment promised a retry that does not exist

trigger: run_dictionary_gc's retry-state wiring, do_purge_source's reply JSON and typed-status precedence, and the stop publication had no test; planner-only and store-only tests survive reverting the plugin wiring
summary: Covered through the real plugin by single-threaded dispatcher cases (raw marker edits and an RAII-guarded latch, no sleep, no thread): fresh status keys, a not-due pass leaving the markers alone, a due pass resetting the streak, a stop leaving every marker alone, and the purge reply and typed status in the stopped, both-pending, WAL-only and rerun states. Mutation-checked (plan ignored, latch not passed, early return removed: each fails a case). The starved branch's three marker writes cannot be driven without a deadline seam and are read-verified, stated in the PR notes.

trigger: a normal agent stop: Agent::stop() ends in thread_pool_.reset() before the plugin shutdown loop, and trigger_engine_.stop() joins the trigger threads before shutdown() on both paths, so a flag set in shutdown() is raised only after the work it was meant to stop has been waited out; the promised stop behaviour is not reachable on that path (shipped-incomplete, not a security control)
summary: The documents said an agent stop ends the purge sweep at once; with the plugin-local stopping_ flag that was false on a normal stop. Fixed by deleting stopping_ and reading the agent-core latch, which Agent::stop() raises before it cancels the stream and before any join, and which every stop_requested_ store pairs with. Wording now states the limits: the sweep ends at its next check, the row delete, a commit and the write-lock wait are not interruptible, and a lost server connection is not a stop. Documents, generated echo.json and PR notes updated.
classification_rationale: the documents promised a behaviour the code did not deliver on a normal stop

trigger: docs/clock-guarded-retention.md said a stop counts as the deadline for the dictionary GC generally, which was true only for purge
summary: Both plugin callers now pass the stop latch, so the sentence is true as written; the row also states that a pass a stop ended is not counted as starved and stamps neither marker.
classification_rationale: the row claimed more than the code did at the time
